review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.

8:1.sourceText: Κεφάλαιον δὲ ἐπὶ τοῖς λεγομένοις, τοιοῦτον ἔχομεν ἀρχιερέα, ὃς ἐκάθισεν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ θρόνου τῆς Μεγαλωσύνης ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς,
8:1.targetText: And the sum concerning the things spoken of [is]: we have such a Chief Priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Greatness in the heavens,

groups.note: The actual κεφάλαιον is the chief point/summary; LSV the sum uses sum in that summarizing sense, not a numerical addition or a different source total noun.
The actual feminine right-side substantive δεξιᾷ denotes the right hand/side; English right hand expresses that real substantive idiom, not a separately written hand noun.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

8:2.sourceText: τῶν ἁγίων λειτουργὸς καὶ τῆς σκηνῆς τῆς ἀληθινῆς, ἣν ἔπηξεν ὁ Κύριος, οὐκ ἄνθρωπος.
8:2.targetText: a servant of the holy places, and of the true dwelling place, which the LORD set up, and not man,

groups.note: The actual neuter plural holy substantive denotes the sanctuary/holy places; English places makes that real substantival reference explicit without a separate Greek place noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual repeated attributive article introduces true as modifier of the same dwelling; LSV expresses that reference with its single definite article in of the true dwelling place, without a second separate article.

unmappedTarget.reason: English inserts the coordinating and in and not man; pinned N1904 has οὐκ ἄνθρωπος without a separate καί connector.

8:3.targetText: for every chief priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices, from where [it is] necessary for this One to also have something that He may offer;

groups.note: The actual εἰς τὸ articular-infinitive construction marks the purpose of appointment; English to expresses the whole purpose connector, not two independently rendered source words.
The actual accusative this-one substantive is the subject of have; English for this One states that same infinitival-subject role without a separately written source for preposition.

8:4.sourceText: εἰ μὲν οὖν ἦν ἐπὶ γῆς, οὐδ’ ἂν ἦν ἱερεύς, ὄντων τῶν προσφερόντων κατὰ νόμον τὰ δῶρα·
8:4.targetText: for if, indeed, He were on earth, He would not be a priest (there being the priests who are offering the gifts according to the Law,

groups.note: The actual οὐδέ has the negative-even force not even; LSV prints not without a separate English even.

The actual articular offering participle designates those who offer; English splits its nominal/relative support into the ... who around the added explicit priests noun. The article is not assigned a priest-noun lemma.

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness connective difference: pinned N1904 has inferential οὖν, then/therefore; LSV for follows the causal γάρ reading. The direction of the discourse relation differs, so the lexical connector identities are kept distinct.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness connective difference: English for follows γάρ, whereas pinned N1904 has οὖν, then/therefore. No causal γάρ identity is invented in the original.

Source-witness explicit role-noun addition: TR prints ἱερέων, priests, in this clause; pinned N1904 has only the substantival those-offering construction. The actual nominalizer and offering predicate are retained, without inventing a written priest noun.

8:5.sourceText: οἵτινες ὑποδείγματι καὶ σκιᾷ λατρεύουσιν τῶν ἐπουρανίων, καθὼς κεχρημάτισται Μωϋσῆς μέλλων ἐπιτελεῖν τὴν σκηνήν. Ὅρα γάρ φησίν, ποιήσεις πάντα κατὰ τὸν τύπον τὸν δειχθέντα σοι ἐν τῷ ὄρει·
8:5.targetText: who to an example and shadow serve of the heavenly things, as Moses has been divinely warned, being about to construct the Dwelling Place, for, “See,” He says, “[that] you will make all things according to the pattern that was shown to you on the mountain”),

groups.note: The actual perfect passive divine-instruction verb κεχρημάτισται is rendered has been divinely warned; its one written predicate supplies that whole divine-warning expression.

The actual completing/bringing-to-completion verb ἐπιτελεῖν concerns constructing the dwelling; LSV to construct keeps that completing-building predicate in context without substituting a different Greek building lemma.

unmappedTarget.reason: English inserts the quoted directive/complement frame that after See; pinned N1904 has the direct future make instruction with no separate that connector.

8:6.sourceText: νῦν δὲ διαφορωτέρας τέτυχεν λειτουργίας, ὅσῳ καὶ κρείττονός ἐστιν διαθήκης μεσίτης, ἥτις ἐπὶ κρείττοσιν ἐπαγγελίαις νενομοθέτηται.
8:6.targetText: but now He has obtained a more excellent service, how much He is also mediator of a better covenant, which has been sanctioned on better promises,

groups.note: The actual perfect passive law-establishing verb νενομοθέτηται is rendered has been sanctioned, meaning formally established under law; it is not a different Greek approval or punishment verb.

8:8.sourceText: μεμφόμενος γὰρ αὐτοὺς λέγει Ἰδοὺ ἡμέραι ἔρχονται, λέγει Κύριος, καὶ συντελέσω ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον Ἰσραὴλ καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον Ἰούδα διαθήκην καινήν,
8:8.targetText: For finding fault, He says to them, “Behold, days come, says the LORD, and I will complete with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah, a new covenant,

groups.note: The actual συντελέω completion verb is used for accomplishing/ratifying the covenant; LSV I will complete retains that real completing head, without substituting the different covenant-making verb used in8:10.

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness case/attachment difference: pinned accusative αὐτούς is the object of finding fault, with them; LSV to them follows the dative reading as recipient of says. The likely same audience does not make these distinct grammatical attachments the same lexical role.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness case/attachment difference: LSV attaches the dative-reading people as recipient of says; pinned N1904 accusative αὐτούς belongs to finding fault. No speech-recipient dative is borrowed from that different attachment.

8:9.targetText: not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers, in the day of My taking [them] by their hand, to bring them out of the land of Egypt—because they did not remain in My covenant, and I did not regard them, says the LORD—

The actual genitive μου identifies the taking participle subject; English My taking recasts that same first-person subject as a gerund possessive.
The actual genitive hand is what is grasped; LSV taking them by their hand recasts the same hand-grasping event with by, not a separately written source by preposition.

8:11.sourceText: καὶ οὐ μὴ διδάξωσιν ἕκαστος τὸν πολίτην αὐτοῦ καὶ ἕκαστος τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, λέγων Γνῶθι τὸν Κύριον, ὅτι πάντες εἰδήσουσίν με ἀπὸ μικροῦ ἕως μεγάλου αὐτῶν.
8:11.targetText: and they will not each teach his neighbor, and each his brother, saying, Know the LORD, because they will all know Me—from the small one of them to the great one of them,

groups.note: The actual οὐ μή is the emphatic negative construction; English not renders its combined negation without inventing a second independent English negative.
The actual substantive small adjective names the small/least person; English the small one supplies its real nominal support without a separate Greek one numeral or person noun.
The actual substantive great adjective names the great/greatest person; English the great one supplies that real nominal support.

The one actual final αὐτῶν is the partitive people relation across the small-to-great range; LSV repeats of them at both endpoints. Both realizations preserve the same actual coordinated-range possessive/partitive identity, not a second printed Greek pronoun.
